extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum evaluators, and researchers interested in middle-school mathematics interventions
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and evaluate a specific middle-school mathematics curriculum intervention (The Expert Mathematician) with respect to program design, instructional materials, alignment to standards, assessment practices, and available research evidence. Intended to inform adoption/decision-making and evidence synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program duration and lesson structure
rubrics_metrics.description: "A three-year program of instruction ... with 196 lessons that teach the 'Logo' programming language. Each lesson ranges from 40-120 minutes, or one to three class periods.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies total program length (three years), number of lessons (196), and the expected class-time per lesson (40–120 minutes / 1–3 class periods) as constraints for implementation and fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional materials and delivery format
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Expert Mathematician coursework combines integrated computer software with workbook activities. The developer used the computer program 'LogoWriter' to develop the curriculum."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights the requirement/expectation of integrated software plus consumable print materials; implementation depends on access to LogoWriter (or equivalent) and ability to integrate software and workbook tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum content coverage and standards alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: "The curriculum... covers general mathematics, pre-algebra, and algebra I. The developer describes the curriculum as covering the range of concepts and content areas in the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics 'Curriculum and Evaluation Standards.'",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should check that lesson content maps to general math, pre-algebra, and Algebra I topics and that it aligns with NCTM standards as claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Built-in assessment practice (unit testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A test of unit concepts is administered at the end of each instructional unit.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program includes formative/summative unit concept tests — fidelity and interpretation of outcomes depend on how these unit tests are administered and scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard compliance (WWC evidence standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The What Works Clearinghouse (WWC) identified only one study on 'The Expert Mathematician' that met its evidence standards.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion in WWC synthesis requires studies to meet WWC evidence standards; evaluators should apply or review those standards (rigor, internal validity) when judging program effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study characteristics and sample size for effectiveness evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: "The one study included 90 eighth-grade students in a middle school in St. Louis, Missouri.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes the small, single-site sample (n=90, eighth grade) underlying the WWC finding — reviewers should consider sample size, representativeness, and context when generalizing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reported program effect on achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: "'The Expert Mathematician' was found to have a potentially positive effect on math achievement.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome label ('potentially positive') indicates limited or tentative positive evidence; users should interpret magnitude and certainty cautiously and consult the underlying study for effect sizes and statistical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and scope of the evidence review
rubrics_metrics.description: "This report updates the previous WWC report on 'The Expert Mathematician' that was released on the WWC website November 2004. This report includes research from the original review. No new studies were identified for this updated report.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the review process and that no additional evidence was found since the prior review — adoption decisions should account for the lack of newer independent studies.
